title: Inquest into man's strange death in Surrey delayed
article: A BC Coroners Service inquest into the death of Ernest Shawn Moosomin was to begin this week but has been reset to Nov. 2 due to scheduling conflicts.
Moosomin, 41, died while in police custody in Whalley last year.

Transit Police arrested Ernest Shawn Moosomin near the Surrey Central bus loop on July 31, 2014. Transit Police spokeswoman Anne Drennan said at the time that Moosomin was taken under the Mental Health Act for "irrational behavior" on a Coast Mountain bus at the bus loop.
"He was rambling incoherently and hiding under a seat in the bus," Drennan told the Now.
She said police asked him if he wanted to be taken to hospital, admitted under the MHA. "He said yes, he would. He was compliant."
The officers drove Moosomin to Surrey Memorial Hospital in a patrol car, to be examined, but upon arrival he was found to be in "medical distress" in the back seat.
"Despite the medical assistance, he was pronounced dead at 39 minutes after midnight."
The inquest will be at Burnaby Coroners Court in Metrotown, with Dr. Kelly Barnard presiding.

Barnard and a jury will hear testimony from witnesses under oath to determine the facts surrounding Moosomin's death and the jury, if required, will then have an opportunity to make recommendations toward preventing similar deaths.
